note: Executable command authority for the EOS quality gate. An agent can choose a project and suite, never a command. `%ENGINE%` and `%WORKSPACE%` are the only path tokens; nothing here records a machine-specific absolute path. A suite with no verified entry point is marked NOT_CONFIGURED so the gate returns BLOCKED instead of a fake green. `interpreters` names an interpreter a suite needs; if it is absent the suite is BLOCKED (the tests did not run), not FAIL.

bighero-venv.description: BigHero's Windows virtual environment (Python 3.11.9 + pytest 9.0.3), verified present 2026-10-19. The system interpreter has no pytest, so this suite cannot run without it.

pass.description: Self-test fixture that must pass. Proves the gate can return PASS.

fail.description: Self-test fixture that must fail. Proves the gate does not rubber-stamp.

blocked.description: Fixture that exits 2. Proves the gate reports BLOCKED (the check could not run) instead of FAIL (the code failed). Differential suites depend on this distinction: a missing baseline must never look like a regression.

mixed.description: One passing and one failing required command. Proves a single failure fails the suite.

optional_failure.description: Passing required command plus a failing optional one. Proves optional steps are recorded without blocking.

timeout.description: Proves a hung command is killed and reported, not waited on forever.

missing_binary.description: Proves a missing executable is a recorded failure, not an exception.

engine.description: Real behavioural suite of the product itself: a full skill-index rebuild followed by the router's 14 routing scenarios plus the registry-scope, one-entry-per-file and verified-badge checks. Discovery runs first because routing resolves skill names against the index it produces; a stale or missing index would make the routing cases fail for the wrong reason.

vnext.description: The vNext enforcement core: EDR state machine (14 cases), challenge ledger (5), typed team runtime (5), differential pytest wrapper (5), and model-probe parsing (3). A failure here means the gate that stops a bad change is itself broken.

deploy.description: Synchronise the product engine into the workspace .agents through the official local installer. The command is fixed in this registry; an agent cannot inject a target or a source. This is the only deploy path the gate knows.

vnext_dev.description: Development-only behavioural suite for the universal runtime. It executes the product tree directly (%WORKSPACE%/engineering-os) so new tools can be verified before deployment. Release gates keep using the fixed 'engine' and 'vnext' suites.

p5.description: P5 mechanical benchmark over real fixture projects: web, backend, python, desktop, security, math, cross-process, new project, multi-project and concurrent writers. No model calls; a model benchmark is a separate conditional stage.

p6.description: Read-only P6 metrics over the gate and P5 artifacts. No gate changes, no model calls.

security.description: Real secret scan over the engine. Fails if a credential-shaped string is committed in the product.

regression.description: Release and permission regressions. The release-gate self-test must reject forged PASS records, mismatched commits, changed gate registries, missing suites and tampered packages. The orchestrator runtime self-test must run real nested processes and prove depth, agent, step, timeout, cancellation and workspace bounds. The permission checks must prove no read-only role can write, delegate or bypass an external-directory denial.

thesis_exit.description: Real project tests: the thesis-exit integration file, run in isolation. Measured 2026-10-19: PASS in 10.3 s alone, but 3 of its tests fail inside the full suite, which means those tests are order/state dependent. Recorded as measured fact, not as a project verdict.

unit.description: Full python_ai unit suite, measured differentially. The 2026-10-19 run (4138 passed / 17 failed / 2 skipped) is why this suite is no longer all-or-nothing: a stored baseline names the known failures, so the gate reports NEW failures and DISAPPEARED tests separately instead of repeating the same red line. Baseline: .agents/registry/failures/bighero-unit.json. A missing baseline is BLOCKED, never a fake green.

35 real test files exist at vpniran/iran_resilient_vpn/tests, but no interpreter can run them: the project .venv was built against a Python 3.13 that is no longer installed, and the machine's default interpreter has no pytest. EOS will not install packages into a user project to make its own gate green. Configure an interpreter and this becomes runnable without changing the tests.

No verified entry point. package.json build is `tsc && vite build`, and the installed node_modules is incomplete (no tsc or vite binary in node_modules/.bin), so `npm run build` cannot be trusted as a gate. src-tauri/Cargo.toml exists, so `cargo test` is a candidate once the crate builds reproducibly.
